title: THE IMMANENCE OF GOD
mv: And He is before all things, and in Him all things consist.
mvp: “And He is before all things, and in Him all things consist.”Colossians 1:17 (NKJV)
assignment: In what area(s) do you want God to show His immanence? Speak to Him now and have faith that He will show up for you (No mark).

b.x: The immanence of God refers to His presence, nearness, and active involvement in His creation and in the lives of His people. It is the biblical truth that God is not distant, or merely observing from afar; He is close, attentive, connected and relational. This is different from His transcendence, which means that God is above, infinitely greater, more powerful, distant and separate from the material universe, existing beyond and utterly distinct from everything He created (Jeremiah 23:23; Isaiah 55:9).

God has always been present with and involved in the world He created, especially with His people. At creation, God formed Adam “from the dust” and breathed life into him (Genesis 2:7). God’s voice was heard “walking in the garden” (Genesis 3:8). The burning bush reveals God’s personal call to Moses (Exodus 3:4) as well as His awareness, compassion, and active response to the affliction of His people (Exodus 3:7). God's presence dwelt among Israel in the tabernacle (Exodus 25:8) and His glory (visibly) filled the temple (1 Kings 8:10-11). David declares God's inescapable nearness: whether in the heavens, depths, or darkness, God is there (Psalm 139:7). 1Kings 19:12 reveals God’s personal and intimate way of speaking to His prophets.

Jesus, becoming God in the flesh (John 1:14), is the ultimate act of divine immanence. “Immanuel” means “God with us” (Matthew 1:23). He came to the earth, walked, talked, healed, cried and ate with people. Jesus promised the Holy Spirit would come to dwell in believers (John 14:17). The Spirit is not just near but indwelling, guiding, and teaching us (John 14:26). Christ remains present with His people through the Holy Spirit (Matthew 28:20). In the New Heavens and New Earth, God will dwell fully and forever with His people (Revelation 21:3). This is the eternal expression of God's immanence.

i: God is accessible - We can pray and hear from Him (1 John 5:14-15).
God is personal - God knows our thoughts, fears, and desires (Psalm 139:1-3).
God is compassionate - He sees suffering and acts accordingly (Exodus 3:7-8).
God disciplines and guides - As a Father does (Hebrews 12:6-7).
God is worthy of worship - Not just as Creator but as a loving Father (Revelation 15:4).

b.x: God is not far from believers in Christ: “…for in Him we live and move and have our being” (Acts 17:27-28).
